graph_value.method: Berkowitz-Bour-Davy-Odling (2000) connectivity parameter P = beta L^D lmin^(1-a)/(a-1) integrated over the domain, computed with this repo's own closed form (src/gems27/topology_theory.py, unit-tested against the paper); a = 2.5000 and D = 1.5662 held at the values fitted on the full catalogue (evidence/graph_report.json), lmin = 2 km, L = 227.319 km (domain-equivalent side). dP is exact for a single merge: dn = [lA+lB+gap >= lmin] - [lA >= lmin] - [lB >= lmin] and P is linear in n.
graph_value.delta_P_is_quantised: dP takes only the values {-1, 0, +1} x P/n_ge because it counts systems above lmin = 2 km; it is an ordinal. The continuous tie-break is delta_second_moment_km2 (change in sum l^2 over systems), and connectivity_rank = |dP| desc, |d(sum l^2)| desc, merged length desc. Disclosed in knowledge/03 Addendum D before the Stage-B gate ran.
graph_value.second_moment_caveat: No critical value is quoted for sum(l^2)/area: a threshold for it could not be verified from an official source inside this sandbox (only github.com and pypi.org are reachable). It is reported as a continuous relative measure and as the tie-break inside equal |dP|, never as a pass/fail criterion.

Structural-setting label (geometry only; mapping to settings is ours): linkage/termination/step-over settings host ~25%/32% of characterised Great Basin geothermal systems (Faulds & Hinz 2015). Connectivity context: the catalogue network is near its critical connectivity (Berkowitz-style P=5.78 vs Pc 5.6-6.0 at the domain scale), where individual closures matter most, but Berkowitz et al. (2000) give ensemble statistics, not a verdict on this particular gap. Base coverage: 100% of its dots already lie within 300 m of the 0.2477 emission. It is a graph bridge: no other selected candidate joins these two sides, so this closure is what actually merges them. Status: validated on both 8-connected component holdout (0.293 vs 0.059 ctrl) and NBMG FID vector-trace holdout (0.100 vs 0.020 ctrl).

NBMG INGENIOUS vector attribution: inter-zone linkage bridging FID=405 ('Grass Valley fault zone', Well Constrained, SLIPSENSE=N, DIPDIRECT=W) to FID=731 ('Pleasant Valley fault zone, Tobin section', Well Constrained, SLIPSENSE=N, DIPDIRECT=W); kinematic_compat=True. Geometry: tip-to-tip along strike; one-sided; the tip points 27 deg off the link and 34 deg. The link strikes N27 E and 50% of the distance-weighted catalogued fault length within ~40 km lies within 20 deg of that strike (data-driven kinematic domain; no external stress model). Structural-setting label (geometry only; mapping to settings is ours): linkage/termination/step-over settings host ~25%/32% of characterised Great Basin geothermal systems (Faulds & Hinz 2015). Connectivity context: the catalogue network is near its critical connectivity (Berkowitz-style P=5.78 vs Pc 5.6-6.0 at the domain scale), where individual closures matter most, but Berkowitz et al. (2000) give ensemble statistics, not a verdict on this particular gap. Base coverage: 0% of its dots already lie within 300 m of the 0.2477 emission.  Graph value (Berkowitz et al. 2000 connectivity parameter, computed on the catalogue graph plus all 345 selected candidates with a=2.500 and D=1.566 held at their fitted values): this closure changes P by dP=+0.0059 (rank 124 of 345 by |dP|) and the largest-system share of total mapped fault length by -0.00000; the merged system would be 3.79 km long. It is a graph bridge: no other selected candidate joins these two sides, so this closure is what actually merges them. Status: validated on both 8-connected component holdout (0.293 vs 0.059 ctrl) and NBMG FID vector-trace holdout (0.100 vs 0.020 ctrl).
